html:
Performers
Clifford Curzon (piano), National Symphony Orchestra (orchestra), Enrique Jordá (conductor) Documented

The Spanish catalogue calls the orchestra the Orquesta Sinfónica Nacional de Londres. Individual players are not identified.

[1] [3]
Work version
Complete work for piano and orchestra, three movements, on six 78-rpm sides Documented

The Internet Archive item lists the three movements and the Spanish catalogue lists the parts on each side. The orchestral edition and any cuts are unknown.

[1] [3]
Recorded
1945-09-26 Documented

Stated in the discographical note of the Internet Archive item. The sources consulted give no second statement of the date.

[1]
Place
Kingsway Hall, London Documented

Stated in the Internet Archive item’s discographical note. A 2021 review places the later LP remake of July 1951 in the same hall.

[1]
Label
Decca Documented

Three 78-rpm discs supplied in an album.

[1] [3]
Catalogue
Decca X 10020–⁠22 (British issue); RG 16051–⁠16053 (Spanish catalogue numbers) Documented

The Internet Archive item gives X 10020–⁠22; the Spanish catalogue of 1954 gives RG 16051–⁠16053 for the same performers and work.

[1] [3]
Matrix, take, sides
Six sides, matrices AR 9689-2, 9690-2, 9691-1, 9692-1, 9693-2, 9694-2; the Spanish catalogue divides the work as Generalife parts 1 and 2, Generalife conclusion, Danza lejana part 1, Danza lejana conclusion with Sierra de Córdoba part 1, and Sierra de Córdoba final Documented

Matrix numbers and side divisions come from two independent listings. Which matrix belongs to which side is not stated.

[1] [3]
Transfer
Satyr 78rpm collection, Internet Archive Documented

The item is in the Internet Archive’s satyr78rpm collection; no personal mastering credit is given.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The item was uploaded on 11 July 2022; the date of the transfer itself is not stated.

[1]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

Equipment, equalisation and restoration settings are not stated. The file is one continuous MP3 of the six sides.

[1]
Composition rights
Falla died on 14 November 1946. Spanish law protects the works of authors who died before 7 December 1987 for life plus 80 years, so his music remains protected in Spain until the end of 2026; arrangements and modern editions carry their own rights Documented

A phonogram term assessment does not clear the composition, an arrangement or a modern score edition.

[6] [7]
Recording rights
Territorial EU phonogram public-domain basis: published no later than 1954, before 1963 Inferred, not documented

The set is listed in Columbia’s Spanish catalogue of discs published up to 1 January 1954, and a 2021 review says Decca remade the work on LP in July 1951 because the 78 set had been so fine, which places the set before 1951. Its actual first issue date is not established here. This is a territorial phonogram basis, not US or worldwide clearance and not a Creative Commons licence.

[1] [3] [4]

Falla, Noches en los jardines de España; Clifford Curzon, piano; National Symphony Orchestra; Enrique Jordá. Decca X 10020–⁠22, Internet Archive transfer. Territorial EU phonogram basis only; Falla’s composition remains protected in Spain until the end of 2026.
